# Dampen the boost a use gives a link

## Intent

A use of a link today gives back every point the link has lost, so a link one day from expiring jumps to the top of the stream as if it were new. One use says the link still matters, but less than a link used steadily. This change makes a use win back a share of the points a link has lost instead of all of them. A link that has lost few points returns close to the top, and a link close to expiry gets a reprieve and a place in the middle of the stream. Each further use moves it higher.

## Goals

- A use of a link wins back `use_boost` percent of the days the link has decayed (default 50), not all of them. With `start_points` 60 and `use_boost` 50, a link used 5 times that has decayed 62 days has 3 points. After one more use it has 60 + 6 − 31 = 35 points, where today it would have 66.
- Points stay computed from values the API returns: `start_points + use_count − whole days since decay_from`. The new link field `decay_from` is the time decay counts from. `last_used_at` keeps meaning the time of the last use or boost.
- Only the first use of a link on a UTC day wins points back. Later uses that day add 1 to `use_count` and nothing else.
- A re-paste, a restore and an unarchive still give back every lost point, as they do today.
- The owner can set `use_boost` from 10 to 100 on the Settings page. At 100, a use behaves exactly as it does today.
- On deploy, no link's points change.

## Non-goals

- Storing points, or recomputing them on a schedule. Points stay computed when read, as package 13 decided.
- Making a use's boost depend on the link's age since it was added, on the kind of use (open, read, snapshot view, MCP open), or on the link's use count.
- Changing how the stream orders links (pinned, then points descending, then `last_used_at` descending, then id descending), or how searches with free words are ranked.
- Changing expiry, removal or the `decay_note` sentences. They follow the new points with no change of their own.
- Showing `decay_from` on the link card. The card keeps "Used <when>" from `last_used_at`.
- Changing the statistics page (packages 18 and 19). It reads points through `pointsAt`, so it follows the new points without a change of its own.

## Background

Points come from package 13 (`13_points_and_expiry`, sealed), and package 14 (`14_keep_links_in_archive`, active) added the archive. Points are never stored. `pointsAt` in `src/worker/decay/note.ts` computes them as `start_points + use_count − whole 24-hour periods since last_used_at`, and two SQL expressions compute them the same way: `POINTS_AT` in `src/worker/links/stream.ts`, which orders the stream, and `expiryStatement` in `src/worker/decay/decay.ts`, which expires links at 0 points or below. Package 18 (`18_show_library_statistics`) counts links by points through `pointsAt`.

Every use (an open, a read, a snapshot view, an MCP open) goes through `recordUse` in `src/worker/links/use.ts`. It adds 1 to `use_count`, sets `last_used_at` to now, makes an expired link `active` and writes a `link_uses` row. So every use gives back every lost point, and the link's points become `start_points + use_count`. Three boosts set `last_used_at` to now without a use: the re-paste (`addStatement` in `src/worker/links/store.ts`), restore (`POST /api/v1/links/{id}/restore`) and unarchive (`POST /api/v1/links/{id}/unarchive`), both in `src/worker/decay/archive.ts`. A new link, whether added or imported (`src/worker/imports/imports.ts`), starts with `last_used_at` set to the time it was added or imported.

`last_used_at` has other readers besides points. The link card shows "Used <when>" from it, the stream breaks ties between equal points with it, searches order by it, and packages 18 and 19 describe it as the last use. So decay cannot simply move `last_used_at` back.

The decay settings are `start_points` (default 60) and `remove_days` (default 180). `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/settings/decay` serve them (`src/worker/decay/routes.ts`), and the Settings page edits them in `DecaySection` (`src/web/pages/DecaySection.tsx`). Today the help text of "Start points" reads "Points a link starts with and goes back to when used, plus one per use; it loses one a day".

## Requirements

### Decay start and points

- Every link has `decay_from`, a timestamp the API returns on every link (in the same form as `last_used_at`; for an archived link too).
- A link's points at time t are `start_points + use_count − max(0, whole 24-hour periods from decay_from to t)`. `pointsAt`, the stream's order, the expiry run and every place that shows points use this one formula. An archived link still has `points: null`.
- A new link, added or imported, has `decay_from` equal to its `last_used_at`.

### A use

- When a use of a link is recorded at time t, and the link's `last_used_at` before the use falls on an earlier UTC day than t:
  - `use_count` goes up by 1 and `last_used_at` becomes t, as today;
  - `decay_from` moves forward by `use_boost` percent of the time from `decay_from` to t: `decay_from' = decay_from + (t − decay_from) × use_boost / 100`, rounded down to the millisecond. At `use_boost` 100, `decay_from` becomes t.
- When the link's `last_used_at` before the use falls on the same UTC day as t, `use_count` goes up by 1 and `last_used_at` becomes t, but `decay_from` does not change. The link's points go up by exactly 1.
- A use of an expired link makes it `active` at once, as today. It also sets `decay_from` to t, whatever `use_boost` is and whatever day the link was last used. Its points become `start_points + use_count`, as a restore makes them.
- A use of an archived link follows the same rule. Its points stay null while it is archived, and an unarchive resets `decay_from` anyway.
- A pinned link and a link in a workspace follow the same rule as any other link.
- Example (start_points 60, use_boost 50): link A has 5 uses and `decay_from` 6 days ago, so 59 points. After a use it has 6 uses and `decay_from` 3 days ago: 63 points. Link B has 5 uses and `decay_from` 62 days ago, so 3 points. After a use it has 6 uses and `decay_from` 31 days ago: 35 points. Opened again a minute later, the same UTC day, B has 36 points.

### Boosts

- A re-paste of an existing link, a restore of an expired link and an unarchive of an archived link set both `last_used_at` and `decay_from` to now. The link's points become `start_points + use_count`, as today.
- Archiving a link does not change `decay_from`.

### The setting

- `GET /api/v1/settings/decay` answers `200 {"start_points": 60, "remove_days": 180, "use_boost": 50}` with the owner's values (defaults shown).
- `PUT /api/v1/settings/decay` takes all three fields. `use_boost` must be a whole number from 10 to 100. `start_points` and `remove_days` keep their range of 7 to 3650.
  - A `use_boost` that is missing, not a whole number, or outside 10 to 100 is refused with `400 {"error": "invalid_threshold", "field": "use_boost", "message": "use_boost must be a whole number from 10 to 100"}`, and nothing is stored.
  - The other refusals are unchanged.
- A change to `use_boost` applies to uses recorded after the change. It does not move any link's `decay_from`, so no link's points change when it is saved.
- The Settings page shows a third field, "Use boost (%)", with the help text "Share of the points a link has lost that a use wins back, once a day. At 100, a use gives back all of them." A refusal is shown beside the field, as the other two show theirs. The help text of "Start points" becomes "Points a link starts with, plus one per use. It loses one a day."
- The account export (`src/worker/account/export.ts`) carries no settings today, and does not carry `use_boost`. Each exported link carries `decay_from`, as every link the API returns does.

### Changing existing data

- When the change is deployed, every link's `decay_from` is set to its `last_used_at`, and every owner's `use_boost` is set to 50. No link's points change on deploy, and no link expires because of the deploy.

### End-to-end flows

1. With `start_points` 60 and `use_boost` 50, the owner has link A (5 uses, `decay_from` 6 days ago) and link B (5 uses, `decay_from` 62 days ago, so 3 points, listed below A). The owner opens B from the stream. B's card shows "expires in 35 days", and the stream lists B below A, where today it would list B first. The owner opens B again the same day. Its card shows "expires in 36 days".
2. The owner sets "Use boost (%)" to 100 on the Settings page and saves. They open a link that has decayed 20 days. Its points become `start_points + use_count`, and the stream lists it at the top of the unpinned links.
3. The owner sets "Use boost (%)" to 5 and saves. The field shows "use_boost must be a whole number from 10 to 100", and `GET /api/v1/settings/decay` still answers the previous value.

## Design Decisions

1. **A use wins back a share of the decayed time, not all of it.** This is the owner's decision. A link close to expiry gets a reprieve without jumping above links in steady use, and repeated uses still bring it back to the top.
2. **The share comes from the time decayed, not from the link's age since it was added.** This is the owner's decision. Scaling by age would stop an old link in steady use from ever reaching the top, and "close to expiry" means time decayed.
3. **Decay counts from a new field, `decay_from`. `last_used_at` keeps its meaning.** The card, the stream's tie-break, the searches and the statistics packages read `last_used_at` as the time of the last use.
4. **Points stay computed, and `decay_from` is returned by the API.** This keeps package 13's decision: the owner can see why a link has its points, from `start_points`, `use_count` and `decay_from`.
5. **`use_boost` is an owner setting, from 10 to 100, default 50.** This is the owner's decision. At 100 the owner gets today's behaviour back, and 10 is the floor, because below it a use would barely count.
6. **Only the first use of a link on a UTC day wins points back. Later uses that day add 1 to the use count.** This is the owner's decision. An open followed by a read are two uses of one visit, and they must not compound to 75%. Package 05 already counted days in UTC.
7. **Re-paste, restore and unarchive keep the full reset.** This is the owner's decision. They are deliberate actions, and a restore of a link that expired long ago would otherwise bring it back at 0 points or below, to expire again at the next run.
8. **A use of an expired link resets its decay in full.** This is the owner's decision. It is a deliberate retrieval, like a restore. The dampened rule would leave it at 0 points or below, so it would expire again at the next run.
9. **A change to `use_boost` applies to later uses only.** Moving every link's `decay_from` when the setting changes would rewrite history the owner cannot see.
10. **Concurrent first uses of a day move `decay_from` once.** Decided in this run: the boost is computed from the row's own values in the statement that counts the use, so a burst of parallel opens behaves like one first use and the rest same-day uses.
11. **Profile: full, in three tasks.** Decided in this run: the change crosses the website, the API and the decay run, with two end-to-end flows, so it needs execution paths; the tasks are the decay start (with the migration), the use rule with the boosts, and the setting.

## Dependencies

- `13_points_and_expiry` (sealed): its points formula and its rule that a use resets points. This PRD supersedes that rule.
- `14_keep_links_in_archive` (active, all tasks done): unarchive resets `decay_from`.
- `05_decay_and_liveness` (active, all tasks done): the decay settings routes and `DecaySection`.
- `01_accounts_links_and_stream` (active, all tasks done): `recordUse` and the re-paste.
- `07_bulk_import` (active, all tasks done): imported links start with `decay_from`.
- `18_show_library_statistics` (active, 2 of 7 tasks done) and `19_record_daily_activity` (active, 0 of 8 done): they read points through `pointsAt` and are not changed. They do not block this work.

## Glossary

- **decay start** (`decay_from`): the time a link's decay counts from. Its points are `start_points + use_count` minus the whole days since then. A boost sets it to now, and so does a use of an expired link. Any other first use on a UTC day moves it forward by `use_boost` percent of the time since.
- **use boost** (`use_boost`): the owner's setting, from 10 to 100 (default 50), for the share of decayed time that the first use of a link on a UTC day wins back.
- **use**, **boost**, **points**, **start points**: as package 13 defines them, except that a use no longer resets points.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Points count from the decay start

**Rationale:** A use can only win back part of the decay if decay counts from a time of its own, while last_used_at keeps meaning the last use.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] THE Alexandria API SHALL return on every link it returns, archived links included, a field decay_from holding the time the link's decay counts from, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp in the same form as last_used_at
   → each link object in a response carries decay_from: string (ISO 8601, millisecond precision, 'Z' suffix)
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, extend the table of 'a link’s points' so seedLinks takes a decayFrom distinct from lastUsedAt: GET /api/v1/links/{id}; assert link.decay_from == seeded decayFrom and link.last_used_at == seeded lastUsedAt; for one archived row assert decay_from is the seeded value and points is null
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] THE Alexandria API SHALL for any link that is not archived, compute its points at time t as start_points + use_count - max(0, whole 24-hour periods from decay_from to t), whatever its last_used_at
   → link.points: integer as computed by pointsAt from start_points, use_count and decay_from; null for an archived link
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts 'a link’s points', the table over {uses, decayed, lastUsed}: {0, 0, now} -> 60; {0, DAY - 60000, now} -> 60; {0, DAY, now} -> 59; {5, 62 DAY, 1 DAY ago} -> 3; {10, 5 DAY, 5 DAY ago} -> 65; {0, 61 DAY, now} -> -1; assert link.points equals the expected value; the case where last_used_at is recent but decay_from is old shows the points follow decay_from
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] THE Alexandria API SHALL order the unpinned links of the stream, and of a search made of filters alone, by points computed from decay_from descending, then last_used_at descending, then id descending
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/links/stream.test.ts, extend 'lists pinned links by position, then the rest by points, last use and id' with two links whose last_used_at order is the reverse of their decay_from order: assert the stream lists them by the points decay_from gives, and two links of equal points by last_used_at descending
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN the scheduled decay evaluation runs for an owner, THE Alexandria API SHALL expire every link at 0 points or below, computed from decay_from, that is active, pending or unreachable, not pinned and in no workspace, and leave every link above 0 points as it was
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts 'expiry by decay', a table: a link with last_used_at today and decay_from 61 days ago (0 uses) expires; a link with last_used_at 61 days ago and decay_from today stays active; assert state and expired_at after evaluateDecay
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] WHEN a link is added through POST /api/v1/links or created by an import, THE Alexandria API SHALL set the new link's decay_from equal to its last_used_at
   → the created link has decay_from == last_used_at, so its points are start_points + 0
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/links/links.test.ts, after POST /api/v1/links adds a new URL assert link.decay_from == link.last_used_at; in src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts 'POST /api/v1/imports adds', for each imported link assert decay_from == last_used_at
   ```

### REQ-2: A use wins back a share of the decay

**Rationale:** One use says a link still matters, but less than steady use, so a link close to expiry gets a reprieve instead of the top of the stream.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a use (an open, a read, a snapshot view or an MCP open) of a link that is not expired is recorded at time t and the link's last_used_at before the use falls on an earlier UTC day than t, THE Alexandria API SHALL add 1 to use_count, set last_used_at to t, and move decay_from forward to decay_from + floor((t - decay_from) * use_boost / 100) milliseconds, where use_boost is the owner's setting
   → the link returned by GET /api/v1/links/{id} after the use has use_count + 1, last_used_at == t, and decay_from as given; its points follow REQ-1.2
   Check: unit
   - setup: start_points 60
   - setup: setNow fixes t at 12:00 UTC
   ```
   in src/worker/links/use.test.ts, a new describe for the boost of a use, recording uses through GET /api/v1/links/{id}/open, a table over {use_boost, uses, decayed} with last use on the previous UTC day: {50, 5, 62 DAY} -> points 35 and decay_from 31 DAY ago; {50, 5, 6 DAY} -> 63 and 3 DAY ago; {100, 3, 20 DAY} -> start_points + 4 and decay_from == t; {10, 0, 30 DAY} -> decay_from moved 3 DAY, points 60 + 1 - 27 = 34; assert use_count, last_used_at == t, decay_from and points
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN a use of a link that is not expired is recorded at time t and the link's last_used_at before the use falls on the same UTC day as t, THE Alexandria API SHALL add 1 to use_count and set last_used_at to t, and leave decay_from unchanged
   → points after the use == points before the use + 1
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/links/use.test.ts beside the table above, a table over the previous last use {t's UTC day at 00:00:00.000, one minute before t}: open the link; assert decay_from unchanged and points == points before + 1; and the boundary case last use at 23:59:59.999 of the previous UTC day with t at 00:00:00.000 does move decay_from
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN a use of an expired link is recorded at time t, THE Alexandria API SHALL make the link active, clear expired_at, add 1 to use_count, and set both last_used_at and decay_from to t, whatever use_boost is and whatever day it was last used
   → GET /api/v1/links/{id} answers state 'active', expired_at null, decay_from == t and points == start_points + use_count
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/links/use.test.ts, extend 'using an expired link' with use_boost 50 and decay_from 200 days ago: open it; assert state 'active', expired_at null, decay_from == t, points == start_points + use_count
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] THE Alexandria API SHALL apply to a pinned link, a link in a workspace and an archived link the same rules for a use as to any other link that is not expired
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/links/use.test.ts, a table over {pinned, in a workspace, archived} each with decay_from 40 days ago and last use on the previous UTC day, use_boost 50: open it; assert decay_from is 20 days before t; for the archived link assert points is null and state stays 'archived'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF several uses of one link are recorded concurrently on a UTC day on which the link had not yet been used or boosted, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL move decay_from once, by the rule of REQ-2.1, and count every use
   → use_count rises by the number of uses; decay_from equals the value a single first use of the day gives

   in src/worker/links/use.test.ts, extend 'counts every one of concurrent opens': a link last used on the previous UTC day with decay_from 40 days ago, use_boost 50, 5 opens in parallel; assert use_count + 5 and decay_from exactly 20 days before t, not further
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] THE Alexandria API SHALL for any recorded use of a link that is not archived, leave its points after the use at least 1 higher than its points just before it

   in src/worker/links/use.test.ts, over generated (use_boost in 10..100, uses in 0..50, decayed in 0..400 days, last use on the same or the previous UTC day, state active or expired): points after open >= points before + 1
   ```

   in src/worker/decay/archive.test.ts, extend 'restoring a link' (brings it back active to the top of the stream) and 'unarchiving a link' (makes it active with its points reset) with decay_from 200 days ago: assert the answer's decay_from == last_used_at == t and points == start_points + use_count

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: The owner uses a link close to expiry and it lands mid-stream

1. **owner** opens the stream on the website, where link B (5 uses, decayed 62 days, 3 points) is listed below link A (5 uses, decayed 6 days, 59 points)
2. **owner** opens link B from its card
3. **website** follows the card's link to GET /api/v1/links/{id}/open
4. **Alexandria API** records the use: use_count 6, last_used_at now, decay_from moved forward by half the time decayed
5. **owner** reloads the stream and sees B's card with 'expires in 35 days', still listed below A
6. **owner** opens link B again the same day and, after reloading, sees 'expires in 36 days'

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, D1

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev serves the website and the Worker
- the owner's use_boost is 50 and start_points 60
- links A and B are added through POST /api/v1/links, opened 5 times each, and their last_used_at and decay_from set with d1() to 6 and 62 days ago

**End state:**

- B's card shows 'expires in 35 days' after the first open and 'expires in 36 days' after the second
- the stream lists A above B
- GET /api/v1/links/{B} answers use_count 7 and decay_from 31 days ago

**Pseudocode:**

```
new test in e2e/decay.spec.ts beside 'the stream lists a much-used link above a recently used one, each with its points': seed with d1(); page.request.get(open B, maxRedirects 0); page.goto('/'); expect cardOf(B) 'expires in 35 days'; assert index(A) < index(B); open B again; reload; expect 'expires in 36 days'; delete both links at the end, as that test does
```

### PATH-2: The owner changes the use boost on the Settings page

1. **owner** opens the Settings page and types 5 into 'Use boost (%)', then saves
2. **website** sends PUT /api/v1/settings/decay with the three fields
3. **Alexandria API** refuses it with 400 invalid_threshold for use_boost and stores nothing
4. **website** shows 'use_boost must be a whole number from 10 to 100' beside the field
5. **owner** types 100 and saves; the website shows 100 after the save
6. **owner** opens a link decayed 20 days, last used on an earlier UTC day, and sees it listed at the top of the unpinned links of the stream

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, D1

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev serves the website and the Worker
- one link added through POST /api/v1/links with last_used_at and decay_from set with d1() to 20 days ago

**End state:**

- GET /api/v1/settings/decay answers use_boost 100
- the link's decay_from equals its last_used_at after the open, and its card is the first unpinned card of the stream

**Pseudocode:**

```
new test in e2e/decay.spec.ts: page.goto('/settings'); fill 'Use boost (%)' with 5; save; expect the error text; fill 100; save; expect value 100; open the link with page.request.get(open, maxRedirects 0); page.goto('/'); assert its card is first; set use_boost back to 50 with PUT and delete the link at the end, because the other specs share this library
```

### 2. Make a use win back a share of the decay, and boosts reset it (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2, REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the task's behaviours to the test files in touches and confirm they fail
- 2.2 In recordUse, in the one UPDATE that counts the use, move decay_from forward by floor((t - decay_from) * use_boost / 100) milliseconds when the link's previous last_used_at falls on an earlier UTC day than t, reading use_boost from the link's user, and leave it unchanged when it falls on the same UTC day; compute both from the row's values in that statement, so concurrent uses of one link move decay_from once
- 2.3 When the link used is expired, make it active, clear expired_at and set decay_from to t, whatever use_boost and the day of its last use
- 2.4 Apply the same rule to pinned links, links in a workspace and archived links; an archived link stays archived with points null
- 2.5 Set decay_from to now, with last_used_at, in the re-paste of an existing link (addStatement in src/worker/links/store.ts), in POST /api/v1/links/{id}/restore and in POST /api/v1/links/{id}/unarchive
- 2.6 Leave decay_from unchanged when a link is archived
- 2.7 Add a property test that a use never raises a link's points by less than 1, over use_boost 10 to 100, use counts, decay lengths and the same or previous UTC day
- 2.8 Add the end-to-end test of PATH-1 to e2e/decay.spec.ts, cleaning up its links as the tests there do
